o: Y así vemos cosas tenidas en poco de algunos, que de otros no lo son.
t: And so we see things held in little esteem by some, which by others are not.

o: ¿Quién piensa que el soldado que es primero del escala, tiene más aborrecido el vivir?
t: Who thinks that the soldier who is first on the ladder has grown more weary of life?

o: No, por cierto; mas el deseo de alabanza le hace ponerse en peligro; y así, en las artes y letras es lo mesmo.
t: No, certainly; but the desire for praise makes him put himself in danger; and so it is in the arts and letters as well.

o: Predica muy bien el presentado, y es hombre que desea mucho el provecho de las ánimas; mas pregunten a su merced si le pesa cuando le dicen: "¡Oh, qué maravillosamente lo ha hecho vuestra reverencia!"
t: The priest preaches very well, and is a man who greatly desires the good of souls; but let them ask his reverence whether it weighs on him when they say: "Oh, how wonderfully your reverence has done it!"

o: Justó muy ruinmente el señor don Fulano, y dio el sayete de armas al truhán, porque le loaba de haber llevado muy buenas lanzas.
t: Don Fulano judged very basely, and gave the blow of arms to the cheat, because he praised him for having carried very good lances.

o: ¿Qué hiciera si fuera verdad?
t: What would he do if it were true?

o: Y todo va desta manera: que confesando yo no ser más santo que mis vecinos, desta nonada, que en este grosero estilo escribo, no me pesará que hayan parte y se huelguen con ello todos los que en ella algún gusto hallaren, y vean que vive un hombre con tantas fortunas, peligros y adversidades.
t: And all goes in this way: since I confess that I am no more holy than my neighbors, in this unpolished style in which I write, it will not weigh on me that they have a share in it, and that all who find some pleasure in it may enjoy it, and see that a man lives with so many fortunes, dangers and adversities.

o: Suplico a vuestra M. reciba el pobre servicio de mano de quien lo hiciera más rico si su poder y deseo se conformaran.
t: I beseech your Majesty to accept the poor service of hand from one who would make him richer if his power and his will were to agree.

o: Cuenta Lázaro su vida, y cuyo hijo fue.
t: Lazarus tells his life, and whose son he was.

o: Pues sepa V.M. ante todas cosas que a mí llaman Lázaro de Tormes, hijo de Tomé González y de Antona Pérez, naturales de Tejares, aldea de Salamanca.
t: Let your Majesty know, above all else, that they call me Lazarus de Tormes, son of Tomé González and Antona Pérez, natives of Tejares, a village of Salamanca.

o: Mi nacimiento fue dentro del río Tormes, por la cual causa tomé el sobrenombre, y fue desta manera.
t: My birth was within the river Tormes, and for that reason I took the surname, and it was in this manner.

o: Mi padre, que Dios perdone, tenía cargo de proveer una molienda de una aceña, que está ribera de aquel río, en la cual fue molinero más de quince años; y estando mi madre una noche en la aceña, preñada de mí, tomóle el parto y parióme allí: de manera que con verdad puedo decir nacido en el río.
t: My father, whom God forgive, had charge of supplying a mill of an olive press, which is on the bank of that river, and he was the miller for more than fifteen years; and one night, when my mother was at the press, pregnant with me, she went into labor and bore me there: so that I can truly say I was born in the river.

o: Pues siendo yo niño de ocho años, achacaron a mi padre ciertas sangrías mal hechas en los costales de los que allí a moler venían, por lo que fue preso, y confesó y no negó y padeció persecución por justicia.
t: Now, when I was a boy of eight years old, certain badly performed bloodletting was blamed on my father in the flanks of those who came there to grind, for which he was imprisoned, and he confessed and did not deny it, and suffered persecution for justice.

o: Espero en Dios que está en la Gloria, pues el Evangelio los llama bienaventurados.
t: I hope in God that he is in Glory, since the Gospel calls them blessed.

o: En este tiempo se hizo cierta armada contra moros, entre los cuales fue mi padre, que a la sazón estaba desterrado por el desastre ya dicho, con cargo de acemilero de un caballero que allá fue, y con su señor, como leal criado, feneció su vida.
t: At that time a certain expedition was made against the Moors, and my father was among them, for he was then banished on account of the misfortune already mentioned, serving as muleteer to a knight who had gone there, and with his master, as a faithful servant, he ended his life.

o: Mi viuda madre, como sin marido y sin abrigo se viese, determinó arrimarse a los buenos por ser uno dellos, y vínose a vivir a la ciudad, y alquiló una casilla, y metióse a guisar de comer a ciertos estudiantes, y lavaba la ropa a ciertos mozos de caballos del Comendador de la Magdalena, de manera que fue frecuentando las caballerizas.
t: My widowed mother, seeing herself without husband and without shelter, determined to draw near to the good people, being one of them herself, and she came to live in the city, and rented a small house, and set herself to cooking for certain students, and she washed the clothes of certain grooms of the Commander of the Magdalena, in such a way that she grew familiar with the stables.

o: Ella y un hombre moreno de aquellos que las bestias curaban, vinieron en conocimiento.
t: She and a dark-skinned man, one of those who tended the beasts, came to know each other.

o: Éste algunas veces se venía a nuestra casa, y se iba a la mañana; otras veces de día llegaba a la puerta, en achaque de comprar huevos, y entrábase en casa.
t: He sometimes used to come to our house and leave in the morning; other times he would arrive at the door on the pretext of buying eggs, and would come into the house.

o: Yo al principio de su entrada, pesábame con él y habíale miedo, viendo el color y mal gesto que tenía; mas de que vi que con su venida mejoraba el comer, fuile queriendo bien, porque siempre traía pan, pedazos de carne, y en el invierno leños, a que nos calentábamos.
t: At first, when he came, I was weighed down by him and was afraid of him, seeing the complexion and the evil look he had; but when I saw that with his coming the food improved, I began to like him, because he always brought bread, pieces of meat, and in winter firewood, with which we warmed ourselves.

o: De manera que, continuando con la posada y conversación, mi madre vino a darme un negrito muy bonito, el cual yo brincaba y ayudaba a calentar.
t: So, going on with the inn and the company, my mother came to give me a very pretty little black boy, whom I would skip about with and help to warm myself.

o: Y acuérdome que, estando el negro de mi padre trebejando con el mozuelo, como el niño vía a mi madre y a mí blancos, y a él no, huía dél con miedo para mi madre, y señalando con el dedo decía: "¡Madre, coco!".
t: And I remember that, while my father's black servant was fooling with the boy, since the child saw my mother and me as white and him not, he fled from him in fear for my mother, pointing with his finger and saying: "Mother, coco!"

o: Respondió él riendo: "¡Hideputa!"
t: He answered, laughing: "¡Hideputa!"

o: Yo, aunque bien mochacho, noté aquella palabra de mi hermanico, y dije entre mí.
t: I, though a mere lad, noticed that word of my little brother, and I said to myself.

o: "¡Cuántos debe de haber en el mundo que huyen de otros porque no se ven a sí mesmos!"
t: "How many there must be in the world who flee from others because they cannot see themselves!"

o: No nos maravillemos de un clérigo ni fraile, porque el uno hurta de los pobres y el otro de casa para sus devotas y para ayuda de otro tanto, cuando a un pobre esclavo el amor le animaba a esto.
t: Let us not marvel at a cleric or a friar, since one steals from the poor and the other from the house, for his devotees and for the help of another such, when love of a poor slave was what prompted him to this.

o: Y probósele cuanto digo y aun más, porque a mí con amenazas me preguntaban, y como niño respondía, y descubría cuanto sabía con miedo, hasta ciertas herraduras que pormandado de mi madre a un herrero vendí.
t: And what I say was proved to him, and more besides, because they questioned me with threats, and as a child I answered, revealing everything I knew in fear, even down to certain horseshoes that my mother had sent me to sell to a blacksmith.

o: Al triste de mi padrastro azotaron y pringaron, y a mi madre pusieron pena por justicia, sobre el acostumbrado centenario, que en casa del sobredicho Comendador no entrase, ni al lastimado Zaide en la suya acogiese.
t: They whipped and tarred my unhappy stepfather, and they put my mother under sentence of justice, on the customary hundred strokes, that she should not enter the house of the aforesaid Commander, nor shelter the wounded Zaide in hers.

o: Él le respondió que así lo haría, y que me recibía no por mozo sino por hijo.
t: He replied that so he would do, and that he received me not as a servant but as a son.

o: Y así le comencé a servir y adestrar a mi nuevo y viejo amo.
t: And so I began to serve and wait on my new and old master.

o: Como estuvimos en Salamanca algunos días, pareciéndole a mi amo que no era la ganancia a su contento, determinó irse de allí; y cuando nos hubimos de partir, yo fui a ver a mi madre, y ambos llorando, me dio su bendición y dijo.
t: As we stayed some days in Salamanca, and it seeming to my master that the profit was not to his liking, he determined to leave there; and when we were about to depart, I went to see my mother, and both of us weeping, she gave me her blessing and said:

o: "Hijo, ya sé que no te veré más.
t: "Son, I know now that I shall see you no more.

o: Procura ser bueno, y Dios te guíe.
t: Try to be good, and God guide you.

o: Criado te he y con buen amo te he puesto. Válete por ti."
t: I have raised you and I have set you with a good master. Make something of yourself."

o: Y así me fui para mi amo, que esperándome estaba.
t: And so I went back to my master, who was waiting for me.

o: Salimos de Salamanca, y llegando a la puente, está a la entrada della un animal de piedra, que casi tiene forma de toro, y el ciego mandóme que llegase cerca del animal, y allí puesto, me dijo.
t: We left Salamanca, and arriving at the bridge, there is at the entrance of it a stone beast, which has almost the shape of a bull, and the blind man ordered me to go close to the beast, and there, once I was, he said:

o: "Lázaro, llega el oído a este toro, y oirás gran ruido dentro dél."
t: "Lázaro, put your ear to this bull, and you will hear a great noise inside it."

o: Yo simplemente llegué, creyendo ser ansí; y como sintió que tenía la cabeza par de la piedra, afirmó recio la mano y diome una gran calabazada en el diablo del toro, que más de tres días me duró el dolor de la cornada, y díjome.
t: I simply drew near, believing it so; and feeling that I had my head as level with the stone, he firmly planted his hand and gave me a great butt in the devil of the bull, and the pain of the goring lasted me more than three days, and he said to me:

o: "Necio, aprende que el mozo del ciego un punto ha de saber más que el diablo", y rió mucho la burla.
t: "Fool, learn that the blind man's servant must know a little more than the devil," and he laughed heartily at the jest.

o: Parecióme que en aquel instante desperté de la simpleza en que como niño dormido estaba. Dije entre mí.
t: It seemed to me that in that instant I awoke from the simplicity in which I had slept as a child. I said to myself:

o: "Verdad dice éste, que me cumple avivar el ojo y avisar, pues solo soy, y pensar cómo me sepa valer."
t: "This one speaks true, for he rouses me to be quick and watchful, since I am all alone, and to think how I may make myself worth something."

o: Comenzamos nuestro camino, y en muy pocos días me mostró jerigonza, y como me viese de buen ingenio, holgábase mucho, y decía.
t: We set out on our journey, and in very few days he showed me his tricks, and seeing that I was of a ready wit, he took great pleasure in it, and would say:

o: "Yo oro ni plata no te lo puedo dar, mas avisos para vivir muchos te mostraré."
t: "Gold or silver I cannot give you, but I will show you how to live a long while."

o: Y fue ansí, que después de Dios éste me dio la vida, y siendo ciego me alumbró y adestró en la carrera de vivir.
t: And so it was that, after God gave me life, He, being blind, enlightened me and guided me along the path of living.

o: Huelgo de contar a V.M. estas niñerías para mostrar cuánta virtud sea saber los hombres subir siendo bajos, y dejarse bajar siendo altos cuánto vicio.
t: I take pleasure in telling Your Grace these trifles, to show how great a virtue it is in men to rise when they are low, and how great a vice it is to let themselves be lowered when they are high.

o: Pues tornando al bueno de mi ciego y contando sus cosas, V.M. sepa que desde que Dios crió el mundo, ninguno formó más astuto ni sagaz.
t: Now, returning to my good blind man and recounting his doings, Your Grace should know that since God created the world, no one formed a more cunning or shrewd man than he.

o: En su oficio era un águila; ciento y tantas oraciones sabía de coro: un tono bajo, reposado y muy sonable que hacía resonar la iglesia donde rezaba, un rostro humilde y devoto que con muy buen continente ponía cuando rezaba, sin hacer gestos ni visajes con boca ni ojos, como otros suelen hacer.
t: In his trade he was an eagle; he knew a hundred and some prayers by heart: a low, calm and very sonorous voice that made the church where he prayed ring out, a humble and devout face which he wore with a very good bearing when he prayed, without making grimaces or contortions with mouth or eyes, as others are wont to do.

o: Allende desto, tenía otras mil formas y maneras para sacar el dinero.
t: Besides this, he had a thousand other ways and means of getting money out of people.

o: Decía saber oraciones para muchos y diversos efectos: para mujeres que no parían, para las que estaban de parto, para las que eran malcasadas, que sus maridos las quisiesen bien; echaba pronósticos a las preñadas, si traía hijo o hija.
t: He said he knew prayers for many and diverse purposes: for women who were not pregnant, for those who were in labor, for those who were unlucky in love and wanted their husbands to love them well; he cast horoscopes for pregnant women, whether they would bear a son or a daughter.

o: Pues en caso de medicina, decía que Galeno no supo la mitad que él para muela, desmayos, males de madre.
t: As for medicine, he said that Galen never knew half as much as he did for toothache, fainting spells, and women's ailments.

o: Finalmente, nadie le decía padecer alguna pasión, que luego no le decía: "Haced esto, hareís estotro, cosed tal yerba, tomad tal raíz."
t: Finally, no one could tell him he suffered from any ailment that he did not immediately prescribe for: "Do this, and I will do that; sew such and such herb, take such and such root."

o: Con esto andábase todo el mundo tras él, especialmente mujeres, que cuanto les decían creían.
t: With this everyone followed him about, especially women, who believed whatever they were told.

o: Destas sacaba él grandes provechos con las artes que digo, y ganaba más en un mes que cien ciegos en un año.
t: From these he drew great profit with the tricks I have described, and he earned in a month more than a hundred blind men earn in a year.

o: Mas también quiero que sepa vuestra merced que, con todo lo que adquiría, jamás tan avariento ni mezquino hombre no vi, tanto que me mataba a mí de hambre, y así no me demediaba de lo necesario.
t: But I would also have your grace know that, with all he was getting, I never saw a man so greedy or so mean, so much so that he was killing me with hunger, and yet he never stinted on what I needed.

o: Digo verdad: si con mi sotileza y buenas mañas no me supiera remediar, muchas veces me finara de hambre; mas con todo su saber y aviso le contaminaba de tal suerte que siempre, o las más veces, me cabía lo más y mejor.
t: I tell you the truth: if I did not know how to make up for it with my cunning and my good tricks, many a time I would have died of hunger; but for all his knowledge and cunning he was so befuddled that always, or most of the time, the biggest and the best share fell to me.

o: Para esto le hacía burlas endiabladas, de las cuales contaré algunas, aunque no todas a mi salvo.
t: For this I made devilish jokes at him, some of which I shall tell, though not all of them at my own risk.

o: Todo lo que podía sisar y hurtar, traía en medias blancas; y cuando le mandaban rezar y le daban blancas, como él carecía de vista, no había el que se la daba amagado con ella, cuando yo la tenía lanzada en la boca y la media aparejada, que por presto que él echaba la mano, ya iba de mi cambio aniquilada en la mitad del justo precio.
t: Everything he could filch and steal he brought home hidden in white stockings; and when they told him to pray and gave him white ones, since he had no sight, there was no one who could hold it over him by threatening him with it, because I had the foot thrust into my mouth and the stocking ready, so that however quickly he reached out his hand, the thing was already mine, cut down to half the fair price.

o: Quejábaseme el mal ciego, porque al tiento luego conocía y sentía que no era blanca entera, y decía.
t: The blind man complained to me, because by touch he soon knew and felt that it was not all white, and he said:

o: "¿Qué diablo es esto, que después que conmigo estás no me dan sino medias blancas, y de antes una blanca y un maravedí hartas veces me pagaban?
t: "What the devil is this? Now that you are with me they give me nothing but white stockings, whereas before they often paid me with a white one and a maravedí?

o: En ti debe estar esta desdicha."
t: This misfortune must lie with you."

o: También él abreviaba el rezar y la mitad de la oración no acababa, porque me tenía mandado que en yéndose el que la mandaba rezar, le tirase por el cabo del capuz.
t: He also cut short his prayers and never finished half the office, because he had ordered me to pull him by the string of his hood as soon as the person who had told him to pray went away.

o: Yo así lo hacía.
t: That's how I did it.

o: Luego él tornaba a dar voces, diciendo: "¿Mandan rezar tal y tal oración?", como suelen decir.
t: Then he would start shouting again, saying: "Are they having us say such-and-such prayers?", as the saying goes.

o: Usaba poner cabe sí un jarrillo de vino cuando comíamos, y yo muy de presto le asía y daba un par de besos callados y tornábale a su lugar.
t: He used to set a little jug of wine beside him when we ate, and I would very quickly snatch it up, give him a couple of silent kisses, and put it back in its place.

o: Mas turóme poco, que en los tragos conocía la falta, y por reservar su vino a salvo nunca después desamparaba el jarro, antes lo tenía por el asa asido; mas no había piedra imán que así trajese a sí como yo con una paja larga de centeno, que para aquel menester tenía hecha, la cual metiéndola en la boca del jarro, chupando el vino lo dejaba a buenas noches.
t: But he caught me out soon, for in the drinking he knew the shortage; and to keep his wine safe, from then on he never let the jug go, but held it fast by the handle. Yet there was no lodestone that drew things to itself as I did with a long rye straw, which I had made for that purpose, and which, put into the mouth of the jug and sucking the wine, left it good night.

o: Mas como fuese el traidor tan astuto, pienso que me sintió, y dende en adelante mudó propósito, y asentaba su jarro entre las piernas, y atapábale con la mano, y ansí bebía seguro.
t: But since the traitor was so cunning, I think he felt me out, and from then on he changed his mind: he set his jug between his legs and held it tight with his hand, and so he drank in safety.

o: Cuando el pobreto iba a beber, no hallaba nada: espantábase, maldecía, daba al diablo el jarro y el vino, no sabiendo qué podía ser.
t: When the poor fellow went to drink, he found nothing there: he was startled, he cursed, he handed the jug and the wine over to the devil, not knowing what it could be.

o: "No diréis, tío, que os lo bebo yo -decía-, pues no le quitáis de la mano."
t: "You won't say, uncle, that I'm the one drinking it," he said, "since you never take it out of his hand."

o: Fue tal el golpecillo, que me desatinó y sacó de sentido, y el jarrazo tan grande, que los pedazos dél se me metieron por la cara, rompiéndomela por muchas partes, y me quebró los dientes, sin los cuales hasta hoy día me quedé.
t: The blow was such that it unsettled me and drove me out of my senses, and the jar was so big that its pieces got into my face, breaking it in many places, and they broke my teeth, without which I have remained to this very day.

o: Desde aquella hora quise mal al mal ciego, y aunque me quería y regalaba y me curaba, bien vi que se había holgado del cruel castigo.
t: From that hour I wished ill on the blind man, and though he fondled and pampered me and looked after me, I saw well enough that he had escaped the cruel punishment.

o: Lavóme con vino las roturas que con los pedazos del jarro me había hecho, y sonriéndose decía: "¿Qué te parece, Lázaro?
t: He washed with wine the breaks that the pieces of the jar had made in me, and smiling he said: "What do you think, Lázaro?

o: Lo que te enfermó te sana y da salud", y otros donaires que a mi.
t: "What made you sick will make you well and give you health," and other jests of his.

o: Ya que estuve medio bueno de mi negra trepa y cardenales, considerando que a pocos golpes tales el cruel ciego ahorraría de mí, quise yo ahorrar dél; mas no lo hice tan presto por hacello más a mi salvo y provecho.
t: Once I was somewhat recovered from my black bruise and lumps, considering that with a few blows like that the cruel blind man would spare me, I wanted to spare him; but I did not do it so quickly, to make it safer and more profitable for me.

o: Y aunque yo quisiera asentar mi corazón y perdonalle el jarrazo, no daba lugar el maltratamiento que el mal ciego dende allí adelante me hacía, que sin causa ni razón me hería, dándome coxcorrones y repelándome.
t: And though I wanted to steady my heart and forgive him for the jar, the mistreatment that the blind man from then on gave me left no room, for without cause or reason he would strike me, dealing me blows on the head and knocking me down.

o: Y si alguno le decía por qué me trataba tan mal, luego contaba el cuento del jarro, diciendo.
t: And if anyone asked him why he treated me so badly, he would immediately tell the story of the jar, saying:

o: "¿Pensaréis que este mi mozo es algún inocente?
t: "Do you think this servant of mine is some sort of innocent?

o: Pues oíd si el demonio ensayara otra tal hazaña."
t: Well, just see if the devil should attempt another such feat."

o: Santiguándose los que lo oían, decían: "¡Mirá, quién pensara de un muchacho tan pequeño tal ruindad!", y reían mucho el artificio, y decíanle: "Castigaldo, castigaldo, que de Dios lo habréis."
t: Those who heard it crossed themselves, saying: "Look at that, who would have thought such wickedness of a lad so small!" And they laughed heartily at the trick, and told him: "Punish him, punish him, for you will have it from God."

o: Y él con aquello nunca otra cosa hacía.
t: And with that he never did anything else.

o: Y en esto yo siempre le llevaba por los peores caminos, y adrede, por le hacer mal y daño: si había piedras, por ellas, si lodo, por lo más alto; que aunque yo no iba por lo más enjuto, holgábame a mí de quebrar un ojo por quebrar dos al que ninguno tenía.
t: And in this I always led him by the worst paths, and on purpose, to do him harm and damage: if there were stones, over them; if mud, by the highest part; for though I did not go by the driest route, it pleased me to break one eye in order to break two of the one who had none.

o: Con esto siempre con el cabo alto del tiento me atentaba el colodrillo, el cual siempre traía lleno de tolondrones y pelado de sus manos; y aunque yo juraba no lo hacer con malicia, sino por no hallar mejor camino, no me aprovechaba ni me creía más: tal era el sentido y el grandísimo entendimiento del traidor.
t: With this he always aimed at my head with the thick end of the staff, which he always brought full of bumps and worn bald by his hands; and though I swore I did not do it out of malice but because I found no better path, he neither benefited nor believed me any longer: such was the cunning and the great understanding of the traitor.

o: Y porque vea V.M. a cuánto se estendía el ingenio deste astuto ciego, contaré un caso de muchos que con él me acaecieron, en el cual me parece dio bien a entender su gran astucia.
t: And so that Your Grace may see how far the wit of this cunning blind man reached, I shall tell one case out of many that happened to me with him, in which it seems to me he gave a good account of his great cunning.

o: Cuando salimos de Salamanca, su motivo fue venir a tierra de Toledo, porque decía ser la gente más rica, aunque no muy limosnera.
t: When we left Salamanca, his reason for coming was to go to the land of Toledo, because he used to say the people there were the richest, though not very charitable.

o: Arrimábase a este refrán: "Más da el duro que el desnudo."
t: He used to lean on this proverb: "Hard cash is worth more than a bare shirt."

o: Y venimos a este camino por los mejores lugares.
t: And we came along this road by the best places.

o: Donde hallaba buena acogida y ganancia, deteníamonos; donde no, a tercero día hacíamos Sant Juan.
t: Where we found good welcome and profit, we stopped; where we did not, on the third day we kept Saint John's.

o: Acaeció que llegando a un lugar que llaman Almorox, al tiempo que cogían las uvas, un vendimiador le dio un racimo dellas en limosna, y como suelen ir los cestos maltratados y también porque la uva en aquel tiempo está muy madura, desgranábasele el racimo en la mano; para echarlo en el fardel tornábase mosto, y lo que a él se llegaba.
t: It happened that, on arriving at a place called Almorox, at the time they were gathering the grapes, a grape-picker gave me a bunch of them as alms, and since the baskets are usually handled roughly, and also because the grape at that season is very ripe, the bunch came apart in my hand; to put it in my knapsack it turned to must, and that was all I got out of it.

o: Acordó de hacer un banquete, ansí por no lo poder llevar como por contentarme, que aquel día me había dado muchos rodillazos y golpes.
t: He decided to give a banquet, both because he could not carry it away and to content me, since that day he had given me many knee-bumps and blows.

o: Sentámonos en un valladar y dijo.
t: We sat down on a fence and he said.

o: "Agora quiero yo usar contigo de una liberalidad, y es que ambos comamos este racimo de uvas, y que hayas dél tanta parte como yo.
t: "Now I want to show you a piece of generosity: let us both eat this bunch of grapes, and you shall have as much of it as I do.

o: Partillo hemos desta manera.
t: We shall divide it this way.

o: tú picarás una vez y yo otra; con tal que me prometas no tomar cada vez más de una uva, yo haré lo mesmo hasta que lo acabemos, y desta suerte no habrá engaño."
t: You shall pick one grape and I another; provided you promise me never to take more than one grape at a time, I will do the same until we finish it, and so there will be no cheating."

o: Hecho ansí el concierto, comenzamos; mas luego al segundo lance; el traidor mudó de propósito y comenzó a tomar de dos en dos, considerando que yo debría hacer lo mismo.
t: The bargain thus made, we began; but at the second round the traitor changed his mind and began taking two at a time, on the reasoning that I ought to do the same.

o: Como vi que él quebraba la postura, no me contenté ir a la par con él, mas aun pasaba adelante: dos a dos, y tres a tres, y como podía las comía.
t: Seeing that he was breaking the agreement, I was not content to keep pace with him, but even went ahead: two by two, and three by three, and I ate as many as I could.

o: Acabado el racimo, estuvo un poco con el escobajo en la mano y meneando la cabeza dijo.
t: When the bunch was finished, he held the stalk a while in his hand and, shaking his head, said.

o: "Lázaro, engañado me has: juraré yo a Dios que has tú comido las uvas tres a tres."
t: "Lázaro, you have fooled me: I swear to God that you ate the grapes three at a time."

o: "No comí -dije yo- mas ¿por qué sospecháis eso?"
t: "I did not eat them three at a time," said I, "but why do you suspect that?"

o: Respondió el sagacísimo ciego.
t: The wisest of blind men replied.

o: "¿Sabes en qué veo que las comiste tres a tres?
t: "Do you know how I know you ate them three at a time?

o: En que comía yo dos a dos y callabas."{, a lo cual yo no respondí.
t: Because I was eating two at a time and you said nothing." To this I gave no answer.

o: Yendo que íbamos ansí por debajo de unos soportales en Escalona, adonde a la sazón estábamos en casa de un zapatero, había muchas sogas y otras cosas que de esparto se hacen, y parte dellas dieron a mi amo en la cabeza; el cual, alzando la mano, tocó en ellas, y viendo lo que era díjome.
t: As we were going thus beneath some arcades in Escalona, where at that moment we were staying in the house of a shoemaker, there were many ropes and other things made of esparto grass, and some of them fell on my master's head; he raised his hand, touched them, and, seeing what they were, said to me.

o: "Anda presto, mochacho; salgamos de entre tan mal manjar, que ahoga sin comerlo."
t: "Come on, lad; let's get out of here, away from such bad fare, which drowns you without your even eating it."

o: Yo, que bien descuidado iba de aquello, miré lo que era, y como no vi sino sogas y cinchas, que no era cosa de comer, díjele.
t: I, who went quite carelessly about that, looked at what it was, and since I saw nothing but ropes and girth-straps, which was no sort of thing to eat, I said so to him.

o: "Tío, ¿por qué decís eso?"
t: "Uncle, why do you say that?"

o: "Calla, sobrino; según las mañas que llevas, lo sabrás y verás como digo verdad."
t: "Silence, nephew; judging by the manner you go about, you will find out and see how I speak the truth."

o: Y ansí pasamos adelante por el mismo portal y llegamos a un mesón, a la puerta del cual había muchos cuernos en la pared, donde ataban los recueros sus bestias.
t: And so we went on through the same gateway and came to an inn, at whose door there were many horns hung on the wall, where the muleteers tied up their beasts.

o: Y como iba tentando si era allí el mesón, adonde él rezaba cada día por la mesonera la oración de la emparedada, asió de un cuerno, y con un gran sospiro dijo.
t: And since I was trying to make out whether that was the inn where he prayed every day for the innkeeper's wife the prayer of the walled-in nun, he seized one of the horns and with a great sigh said:

o: "¡O mala cosa, peor que tienes la hechura!
t: "Oh, wretched thing, worse than the shape you bear!

o: ¡De cuántos eres deseado poner tu nombre sobre cabeza ajena y de cuán pocos tenerte ni aun oír tu nombre, por ninguna vía!"
t: How many men there are who long to put your name upon another's head, and how few who would have you, not even to hear your name, by any means!"

o: Como le oí lo que decía, dije.
t: When I heard what he was saying, I said:

o: "Tío, ¿qué es eso que decís?"
t: "Uncle, what is that you are saying?"

o: "Calla, sobrino, que algún día te dará éste, que en la mano tengo, alguna mala comida y cena."
t: "Silence, nephew; one day this one that I hold in my hand will give you a bad supper and a bad dinner."

o: "No le comeré yo -dije- y no me la dará."
t: "I shall not eat it," I said, "and he will not give it to me."

o: "Yo te digo verdad; si no, verlo has, si vives."
t: "I tell you the truth; if not, you will see it, if you live long enough."

o: Y ansí pasamos adelante hasta la puerta del mesón, adonde pluguiere a Dios nunca allá llegáramos, según lo que me sucedía en él.
t: And so we went on to the door of the inn, where God pleased we should never arrive, judging by what was happening to me there.

o: Era todo lo más que rezaba por mesoneras y por bodegoneras y turroneras y rameras y ansí por semejantes mujercillas, que por hombre casi nunca le vi decir oración.}.
t: He prayed for nothing but innkeepers' wives and tapsters' wives and nougat-sellers' wives and washerwomen and the like sort of women; for a man I hardly ever heard him say a prayer.

o: Reíme entre mí, y aunque mochacho noté mucho la discreta consideración del ciego.
t: I laughed within myself, and though I was but a lad I much appreciated the blind man's discreet thoughtfulness.

o: Mas por no ser prolijo dejo de contar muchas cosas, así graciosas como de notar, que con este mi primer amo me acaecieron, y quiero decir el despidiente y con él acabar.
t: But, to avoid being prolix, I leave off telling many things, both so comical as to be worth noting, that befell me with this my first master; and I mean to speak of the farewell and my ending with him.

o: Estábamos en Escalona, villa del duque della, en un mesón, y dióme un pedazo de longaniza que la asase.
t: We were in Escalona, the duke's town, at an inn, and he gave me a piece of sausage to fry.

o: Ya que la longaniza había pringado y comídose las pringadas, sacó un maravedí de la bolsa y mandó que fuese por él de vino a la taberna.
t: Once the sausage had spattered its fat and eaten up the spatterings, he took a maravedí out of his purse and ordered that wine be brought for it from the tavern.

o: Púsome el demonio el aparejo delante los ojos, el cual, como suelen decir, hace al ladrón, y fue que había cabe el fuego un nabo pequeño, larguillo y ruinoso, y tal que, por no ser para la olla, debió ser echado allí.
t: The devil set the contrivance before my eyes, which, as the saying goes, makes the thief; and it was that by the fire there lay a small turnip, longish and shriveled, such that, since it was not fit for the pot, it must have been thrown there.

o: Yo fui por el vino, con el cual no tardé en despachar la longaniza, y cuando vine hallé al pecador del ciego que tenía entre dos rebanadas apretado el nabo, al cual aún no había conocido por no lo haber tentado con la mano.
t: I went for the wine, and with it I did not take long to dispatch the sausage; and when I came back I found the sinful blind man holding the turnip squeezed between two slices, which he had not yet gotten to know because he had not tried it with his hand.

o: Como tomase las rebanadas y mordiese en ellas pensando también llevar parte de la longaniza, hallóse en frío con el frío nabo. Alteróse y dijo.
t: As he took the slices and bit into them, thinking also to get a share of the sausage, he found himself cold with the cold turnip. He was upset and said:

o: "¿Qué es esto, Lazarillo?"
t: "What is this, Lazarillo?"

o: "¡Lacerado de mí!
t: "Wretch that I am!",

o: -dije yo-. ¿Si queréis a mí échar algo?
t: said I. "Do you want me to put something in it?"

o: ¿Yo no vengo de traer el vino?
t: "Didn't I come bringing the wine?"

o: Alguno estaba ahí, y por burlar haría esto."
t: Someone was there, and to make fun of me he did this."

o: "No, no -dijo él-, que yo no he dejado el asador de la mano; no es posible "
t: "No, no," he said, "I haven't let go of the spit; it's not possible..."

o: Yo torné a jurar y perjurar que estaba libre de aquel trueco y cambio; mas poco me aprovechó, pues a las astucias del maldito ciego nada se le escondía.
t: I swore and forswore again that I was innocent of that exchange and switch; but it served me little, for nothing escaped the cunning of the accursed blind man.

o: ¡Oh, gran Dios, quién estuviera aquella hora sepultado, que muerto ya lo estaba!
t: Oh, great God, if only I had been buried at that hour, for I was as good as dead!

o: Fue tal el coraje del perverso ciego que, si al ruido no acudieran, pienso no me dejara con la vida.
t: The perverse blind man was so bold that, if they had not come at the noise, I think he would not have left me alive.

o: Sacáronme de entre sus manos, dejándoselas llenas de aquellos pocos cabellos que tenía, arañada la cara y rascuñado el pescuezo y la garganta; y esto bien lo merecía, pues por su maldad me venían tantas persecuciones.
t: They pulled me out of his hands, leaving them full of the few hairs he had, my face scratched and my neck and throat scraped; and I well deserved it, for so much persecution came upon me because of his wickedness.

o: Contaba el mal ciego a todos cuantos allí se allegaban mis desastres, y dábales cuenta una y otra vez, así de la del jarro como de la del racimo, y agora de lo presente.
t: The blind man told everyone who came gathering there of my misfortunes, giving an account of them over and over, both of the jug and of the bunch of grapes, and now of what had just happened.

o: Era la risa de todos tan grande que toda la gente que por la calle pasaba entraba a ver la fiesta; mas con tanta gracia y donaire recontaba el ciego mis hazañas que, aunque yo estaba tan maltratado y llorando, me parecía que hacía sinjusticia en no se las reír.
t: Everyone's laughter was so loud that all the people passing along the street came in to see the show; but with such grace and wit did the blind man recount my exploits that, though I was so ill-treated and crying, it seemed to me unjust not to laugh at them with him.

o: Pluguiera a Dios que lo hubiera hecho, que eso fuera así que así.
t: God grant I had done so, for that would have been just as it was.

o: Hiciéronnos amigos la mesonera y los que allí estaban, y con el vino que para beber le había traído, laváronme la cara y la garganta, sobre lo cual discantaba el mal ciego donaires, diciendo.
t: The innkeeper's wife and those who were there became friends with us, and with the wine I had brought him to drink they washed my face and throat, over which the blind man kept making witty remarks, saying:

o: "Por verdad, más vino me gasta este mozo en lavatorios al cabo del año que yo bebo en dos.
t: "Honestly, this lad spends more wine on washings in a year than I drink in two.

o: A lo menos, Lázaro, eres en más cargo al vino que a tu padre, porque él una vez te engendró, mas el vino mil te ha dado la vida."
t: "At least, Lázaro, you are more in debt to the wine than to your father, because he begot you once, but the wine has given you life a thousand times."

o: Y luego contaba cuántas veces me había descalabrado y harpado la cara, y con vino luego sanaba.
t: And then he would tell how many times he had knocked me on the head and scratched my face, and then healed them with wine.

o: "Yo te digo -dijo- que si un hombre en el mundo ha de ser bienaventurado con vino, que serás tú."
t: "I tell you," he said, "that if any man in the world is to be blessed with wine, it will be you."

o: Y reían mucho los que me lavaban con esto, aunque yo renegaba.
t: And those who washed me with this laughed a lot at me, though I cursed.

o: Mas el pronóstico del ciego no salió mentiroso, y después acá muchas veces me acuerdo de aquel hombre, que sin duda debía tener spíritu de profecía, y me pesa de los sinsabores que le hice, aunque bien se lo pagué, considerando lo que aquel día me dijo salirme tan verdadero como adelante V.M. oirá.
t: But the blind man's prediction proved no lie, and afterwards here I often think of that man, who must undoubtedly have had the spirit of prophecy, and I regret the bitter words I gave him, though well I paid him back for them, considering how true what he told me that day turned out to be, as Your Grace will hear further on.

o: Visto esto y las malas burlas que el ciego burlaba de mí, determiné de todo en todo dejalle, y como lo traía pensado y lo tenía en voluntad, con este postrer juego que me hizo afirmélo más.
t: Seeing this, and the bad jibes the blind man made at me, I determined to leave him once and for all, and since I had it planned and it was in my will, this last game he played with me confirmed me in it.

o: Y fue ansí, que luego otro día salimos por la villa a pedir limosna, y había llovido mucho la noche antes; y porque el día también llovía, y andaba rezando debajo de unos portales que en aquel pueblo había, donde no nos mojamos; mas como la noche se venía y el llover no cesaba, dijóme el ciego.
t: And so it was that another day we went out through the town to beg alms, and it had rained heavily the night before; and because it was raining during the day too, I was praying under some of the arcades that the town had, where we did not get wet; but as night was coming on and the rain did not cease, the blind man said to me.

o: "Lázaro, esta agua es muy porfiada, y cuanto la noche más cierra, más recia.
t: "Lázaro, this water is very stubborn, and the darker the night gets, the harder it falls.

o: Acojámonos a la posada con tiempo."
t: Let us take shelter at the inn in good time."

o: Para ir allá, habíamos de pasar un arroyo que con la mucha agua iba grande. Yo le dije.
t: To get there, we had to cross a stream that, with all the water, was running high. I told him.

o: "Tío, el arroyo va muy ancho; mas si queréis, yo veo por donde travesemos más aína sin nos mojar, porque se estrecha allí mucho, y saltando pasaremos a pie enjuto."
t: "Uncle, the stream runs very wide; but if you wish, I see a place where we can cross more quickly without getting wet, because it narrows a great deal there, and with a jump we shall pass over with dry feet."

o: Parecióle buen consejo y dijo.
t: The advice seemed good to him, and he said.

o: "Discreto eres; por esto te quiero bien.
t: "You are discreet; for that I love you well.

o: Llévame a ese lugar donde el arroyo se ensangosta, que agora es invierno y sabe mal el agua, y más llevar los pies mojados."
t: Take me to that place where the stream narrows, for now it is winter and the water is bad, and worse still to go with wet feet."

o: Yo, que vi el aparejo a mi deseo, saquéle debajo de los portales, y llevélo derecho de un pilar o poste de piedra que en la plaza estaba, sobre la cual y sobre otros cargaban saledizos de aquellas casas, y dígole.
t: Seeing the arrangement suited my purpose, I took him out from under the arcades and led him straight to a pillar or stone post that stood in the square, on which and on others the jetties of those houses rested, and I said to him.

o: "Tio, éste es el paso más angosto que en el arroyo hay."
t: "Uncle, this is the narrowest crossing the stream has."

o: Como llovía recio, y el triste se mojaba, y con la priesa que llevábamos de salir del agua que encima de nos caía, y lo más principal, porque Dios le cegó aquella hora el entendimiento (fue por darme dél venganza), creyóse de mí y dijo.
t: Since it was raining hard, and the poor man was getting wet, and with the haste we had to get out of the water that was falling on us, and above all, because God blinded his understanding at that hour (it was to give me my revenge on him), he trusted me and said.

o: "Ponme bien derecho, y salta tú el arroyo."
t: "Set me up straight, and you jump the stream."

o: Yo le puse bien derecho enfrente del pilar, y doy un salto y póngome detrás del poste como quien espera tope de toro, y díjele.
t: I set him up straight facing the post, and I take a jump and put myself behind the post like one who waits for the charge of a bull, and I said to him.

o: "¡Sus! Saltá todo lo que podáis, porque deis deste cabo del agua."
t: "Ho there! Jump all you can, so that you get off this side of the water."

o: Aun apenas lo había acabado de decir cuando se abalanza el pobre ciego como cabrón, y de toda su fuerza arremete, tomando un paso atrás de la corrida para hacer mayor salto, y da con la cabeza en el poste, que sonó tan recio como si diera con una gran calabaza, y cayó luego para atrás, medio muerto y hendida la cabeza.
t: He had scarcely finished saying it when the poor blind man rushed forward like a billy goat, and with all his strength he charged, taking a step back from the run to make a greater leap, and he struck his head against the post, which sounded as loud as if he had hit it with a great gourd, and he fell straight back, half dead with his head split open.

o: "¿Cómo, y olistes la longaniza y no el poste?
t: "How now, did you smell the sausage and not the post?"

o: ¡Olé! ¡Olé! -le dije yo.
t: "Olé! Olé!" said I.

o: Y dejéle en poder de mucha gente que lo había ido a socorrer, y tomé la puerta de la villa en los pies de un trote, y antes que la noche viniese di conmigo en Torrijos.
t: And I left him in the hands of the many people who had come to help him, and I took the gate of the town at a trot, and before nightfall I arrived in Torrijos.

o: No supe más lo que Dios dél hizo, ni curé de lo saber.
t: I learned nothing further about what God made of him, nor did I care to know.
